sections.h2: How the tax bill is figured
sections.html:
Your Shelby County property tax equals the assessed value of the parcel multiplied by the millage rates of every taxing body that covers it. A mill is one tenth of one cent. The rates differ by city, school district and any special district, so the county tax office is the place to get the millage for your parcel.

A bill goes up in two ways: a taxing authority raises its millage, or the appraised value rises through a court-ordered reappraisal or a market increase. Alabama counties now reappraise every year, reviewing one quarter of the county annually, so each parcel is looked at over a four-year cycle.

Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. If a bill goes unpaid, the process moves along a set schedule.

DateWhat happens to the tax bill
October 1Taxes due
December 31Last day to pay before delinquency; last day to report improvements made by October 1
January 1Unpaid taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilProperty advertised for sale
MayTax sale

Counties do not have to mail notices. The bill is a courtesy, and you owe the tax whether or not one arrives, so call the office if you have not seen one by fall.

By December 31, visit the county revenue office and sign a new assessment for any improvement or removal made on or before October 1 of that year. Reportable work includes new structures and additions, pools, remodeling, an added bath or fireplace, a patio, deck, carport or garage.

Normal upkeep does not count. Re-roofing, minor repairs and painting need no reassessment. Selling soon? Keep a record of any work that fits the first list, because an unreported addition can surface later as a corrected assessment.

Alabama defines a homestead as a single-family, owner-occupied dwelling and its land, up to 160 acres, lived in as the primary residence on the first day of the tax year. Owners over 65, permanently and totally disabled owners and blind owners are exempt from the state portion of the tax, though county taxes may still be due.

File for an exemption at the county office, and ask that office for Shelby's own exemption amounts. The exemption follows the owner who lives in the home on the first day of the tax year, so a buyer who moves in applies for their own.

For a purchase, the state's steps are short: record the deed at the probate office, then assess the property at the county revenue office and bring the deed. Make sure the year's taxes are paid, and expect that the bill may still carry the previous owner's name. The new owner is responsible for taxes on property they own whatever name is on the bill.

As a seller, make sure the closing statement says who pays the current year's tax. Report an address change to the county office in writing as well. If you think your assessment is wrong, ask the county tax office for the appeal form and the filing deadline before you list the house.

You can still sell. The clock keeps running, though. A bill unpaid by December 31 turns delinquent on January 1 and moves toward the probate court and a possible May tax sale, so the sooner you learn about a balance, the more choices you have.

If a balance is due at closing, the contract and the closing agent can arrange payment out of the sale proceeds. A cash sale can close on a short schedule, which helps near a deadline, and a firm date is set after the title is reviewed.

  • Ask the county tax office for the payoff on every year that shows a balance.
  • Check whether any improvement was left unreported.
  • Keep proof of any exemption you held in case the office asks.

The steps at closing are the same whether the buyer pays cash or uses a loan. The title company confirms who owns the house and what is owed, collects the payoffs from your proceeds and records the deed at the probate office. You sign, and what remains is paid to you.

sections.h2: Documents to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Collect the deed, your most recent tax bill, any mortgage statement and a photo ID. If you made improvements, find the permits and dates. If you held a homestead exemption, find the confirmation. If the owner has died, bring the estate paperwork showing who can sign.

With these in hand, the title company can give you a clear payoff and a firm closing date much sooner.

Shelby County is in central Alabama, covers 810 square miles and has Columbiana as its seat. Alabaster is the largest city. The county had 223,024 residents in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 238,552.

Its incorporated places include Alabaster, Calera, Chelsea, Columbiana, Helena, Montevallo, Pelham, Westover, Harpersville, Indian Springs Village, Wilsonville and Wilton. Birmingham, Hoover, Leeds, Vestavia Hills and Vincent have parts inside the county but extend into neighboring ones, so confirm which county's records cover your parcel.

Interstate 65 and U.S. 31 run north to south, and U.S. 231 and U.S. 280 cross the east. Commercial flights use Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport in neighboring Jefferson County, and the Shelby County Airport handles general aviation.

Four public systems serve the county: Shelby County Schools, Alabaster City Schools, Pelham City Schools and Hoover City Schools. Private schools include Briarwood Christian School and Indian Springs School. The district depends on the address, so check with the school systems before you tell a buyer.

Buyers recognize Oak Mountain State Park, Oak Mountain Amphitheatre, Cahaba River Wildlife Management Area, the Aldrich Coal Mine Museum, the Heart of Dixie Railroad Museum, Shelby Iron Works Park and American Village. A cash sale does not change the property tax steps. The buyer takes the house as is, taxes are settled at closing as the contract says, and the new owner reports the deed to the probate office.

faqs.q: When are Shelby County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, and they become delinquent after December 31. Unpaid taxes can go to a tax sale the following May.

faqs.q: Do I still owe tax if I never got a bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Counties are not required to mail notices, so the tax is owed regardless.

faqs.q: What work on my Shelby County house has to be reported?
faqs.a: New structures, additions, pools, remodeling, added baths or fireplaces, patios, decks, carports and garages. Re-roofing, painting and minor repairs do not need a reassessment. The deadline is December 31 for work done on or before October 1.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax when a Shelby County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The new owner answers for taxes on property they own, even if the bill carries the old owner's name. The sale contract sets how the year is divided between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Shelby County assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the county tax office for the appeal form and the filing deadline.
